# Results — Study 408 (Three Black Crows)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **three
black crows mark a top and a crash is coming** — tested as a clean signed-**short** event
study on a fixed **30-name liquid large-cap + SPY** basket. For every confirming bar we enter
the next open (one lag), hold 1 / 3 / 5 / 10 days short, and measure the signed return against
zero and against a coin-flip placebo. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, `auto_adjust=True` — 30 long-listed liquid US large-caps + **SPY** (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-18** (last bar in the cached basket) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-18 (**21.5** years; **161,970** total bars) |
| Fingerprint | `bf1d6cb7ca54` (sha1[:12] of the basket closes, `data.fingerprint`) |
| Detector | precise real-body three-black-crows on bars (t−2, t−1, t); strict + prior-uptrend variants for the myth-check |
| Timing / costs | confirm at close of t; enter the **next open** (one lag); hold 1/3/5/10 days **short**; **5 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip) + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short over the hold |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis — and it cuts the *right* way).** The basket is 30
> names that are *still trading* in 2026. A fixed surviving-names panel **excludes the firms
> that actually crashed and delisted** — exactly the cases a "three black crows → crash"
> believer would point to. So this universe is biased **toward** finding a working bearish
> signal. It still finds none, which makes the null verdict strong rather than an artefact of
> selection.

## The signal — signed-SHORT forward return after three black crows

A real "crash" signal needs a **positive** signed-short mean (the short pays) with HAC
*t* ≥ **+2**. The base column is the unconditional (long) forward return; the placebo *p* is
the share of 5,000 coin-flip random picks whose mean **beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n events | signed-short mean | base (long) | win-rate | HAC *t* | one-sample *t* | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 1,530 | **−0.054%** | +0.028% | 47% | −1.60 | −1.58 | −0.73 | 0.942 | −0.156% |
| 3-day  | 1,530 | **−0.117%** | +0.141% | 47% | −1.52 | −1.69 | +0.35 | 0.958 | −0.223% |
| 5-day  | 1,530 | **−0.165%** | +0.253% | 47% | −1.65 | −1.87 | +0.99 | 0.969 | −0.275% |
| 10-day | 1,526 | **−0.284%** | +0.530% | 44% | **−2.06** | −2.23 | +1.92 | 0.984 | −0.404% |

Read it carefully. The signed-short return is **negative at every horizon** and gets *worse*
with the hold (−0.05% → −0.28%). The HAC and one-sample *t* are **negative** — the only
horizon that nears significance (10-day, HAC *t* = −2.06) is significant in the **bounce**
(bullish) direction, the exact opposite of the bearish claim. The coin-flip placebo *p* is
~0.94–0.98: about **95%+ of random picks did better** than shorting the actual crows. There is
no bearish edge here.

## Costs — the loss only deepens

Each event is a fresh short round trip: **5 bps one-way × 2** plus **50 bps/yr** borrow over
the hold. When the gross is already negative, costs can only bury it further.

| horizon | gross short | net of costs + borrow |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | −0.054% | **−0.156%** |
| 3-day  | −0.117% | **−0.223%** |
| 5-day  | −0.165% | **−0.275%** |
| 10-day | −0.284% | **−0.404%** |

There is no horizon where the short clears zero, let alone its costs. There is nothing under
the signal to charge costs *against* — a textbook **Mirage**.

## Myth check #1 — the strict long-bodied crow

Tighten the rule to the purist's crow (long bodies, close near each bar's low). If the lore
hid in a "cleaner" pattern, this should be *more* bearish. It isn't (and the events are rare):

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 145 | +0.060% | +0.65 | 0.302 | −0.042% |
| 3-day  | 145 | −0.093% | −0.47 | 0.669 | −0.199% |
| 5-day  | 145 | −0.081% | −0.33 | 0.616 | −0.191% |
| 10-day | 144 | −0.232% | −0.56 | 0.716 | −0.352% |

## Myth check #2 — only crows after a prior uptrend (a genuine reversal)

A three-black-crows is *supposed* to reverse a rally. Restrict to crows that followed a prior
uptrend (close at t−3 above its level 10 days earlier). Still nothing:

| horizon | n | signed-short mean | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 870 | −0.020% | −0.46 | 0.647 | −0.122% |
| 3-day  | 870 | −0.056% | −0.66 | 0.734 | −0.161% |
| 5-day  | 870 | −0.007% | −0.06 | 0.527 | −0.117% |
| 10-day | 866 | −0.156% | −1.00 | 0.828 | −0.275% |

Neither the strict shape nor the reversal filter produces a bearish edge. The pattern's
predictive content is indistinguishable from noise under every reasonable definition.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic OHLCV panel with a *planted* post-pattern crash, the signed-short inference
behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge (per day) | planted days | n events | signed-short mean (5d) | HAC *t* | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no edge) | 675 | 673 | −0.139% | −1.05 | −1.15 | 0.876 | 49% |
| **+0.004** (planted crash) | 718 | 716 | +0.404% | **+3.02** | +3.41 | 0.000 | 54% |
| **+0.008** (large planted crash) | 754 | 752 | +0.971% | **+7.04** | +8.21 | 0.000 | 61% |

With **no** planted crash the test sits at *t* ≈ 0 (it does not manufacture a bearish edge
from noise); a planted crash lights up the signed-short *t* monotonically. The detector
*would* catch a real post-crows crash if one existed — so the real-tape *t* < 0 is a genuine
**absence** of bearish signal, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Shorting three black crows produces a **negative** signed return at every
  horizon (−0.054% at 1d → −0.284% at 10d) with **negative** HAC *t* (never near +2) and a
  coin-flip placebo *p* ≈ 0.94–0.98 (the real signal sits in the *left* tail). No bearish edge
  exists. Carries an explicit **survivorship** caveat that tilts the test *toward* the claim —
  and it still fails. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The short is **negative gross**; net of the round-trip cost +
  short borrow it is worse at every horizon (−0.275% net at 5d). There is no edge to charge
  costs against. Not FRAGILE — there is simply nothing there.
- **"Crash incoming"? — BUSTED.** The "sell-off is just starting" reading is **backwards**:
  three big red days are a stock that already fell, and it tends to drift mildly **back up**
  (the short loses; the only borderline significance, 10d *t* = −2.06, is the *bounce*).
  Strict-crow and prior-uptrend filters do not rescue it. The famous crash signal is a story
  the chart tells, not one the tape confirms.
